title: Geo-fence commit-fencing and forensic evidence bundles for private deployments
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) require strict guarantees that data does not cross jurisdictional boundaries and that any regional failover is governed by policy gates. Current failover triggers and evacuation actions lack a signed commit-fencing mechanism and do not generate a standardized forensic bundle that proves which nodes were active, what data was moved, and the exact configuration at time-of-switch.

Goal: Implement a geo-fence-aware commit-fencing layer that:
  - Prevents automatic promotion of nodes or replicas outside allowed regions without an auditable approval token.
  - Emits a deterministic forensic evidence bundle on any failover/evacuation, including signed node attestations, retention policy snapshots, and transfer manifests.
  - Integrates with Private control plane (customer VPC) and with our evidence-export pipeline so compliance teams can ingest artifacts automatically.

Scope:
  - Implement the commit-fencing protocol and approval token flow for Private and VPC deployments.
  - Generate a standardized forensic bundle (JSON + compressed logs + signatures) on any region failover, scheduled evacuation, or forced migration.
  - Add console controls to configure geo-affinity gates and emergency override workflows.
  - Wire evidence bundles into the existing evidence-exporter service for long-term storage and customer retrieval.

Out of scope: automated cross-region live migration of KV caches, full legal attestation workflows, or changes to hosted (public) runtime behavior.

Design notes:
  - Commit-fencing: a lightweight two-key model. A local node must hold an active lease and a region token. Before promotion to primary in a new region, a signed approval token from the control plane (or a local on-prem policy engine) is required. Tokens are time-limited and include region, node-id, and policy-hash.
  - Forensic bundle: a deterministic package containing: node identity certs, KVM snapshots metadata (not raw keys), retention policy versions, routing decisions, sequence numbers, and a manifest of S3/Blob URIs for logs. Bundle must be signed by local HSM/KMS and have a canonical JSON manifest for verification.
  - Evidence export: bundles are written to a write-once customer-controlled bucket (or locally retained for air-gapped installs) and a pointer is POSTed to the evidence-exporter with SHA256 checksums.

Telemetry & observability:
  - New metrics: fence_token_issued, fence_token_rejected, forensic_bundle_created, forensic_bundle_upload_failed.
  - Traces on failover path with tags: region_from, region_to, policy_id, token_id.
  - Alerting: P1 alert if forensic bundle creation fails for >95% of failovers in a 1h window.

Rollout plan:
  1) Implement fencing library and unit tests behind feature flag (runtime-2.4).
  2) Integrate with Private control plane in staging; run chaos tests (scheduled evacuation, node kill) in canary customer clusters.
  3) Enable evidence-exporter integration and verify bundles are ingestible in compliance pipelines.
  4) Expose controls in Console as guarded feature with audit logs.

Success criteria: All canary failovers produce verifiable forensic bundles, no automated promotion outside allowed regions, and customers can retrieve bundle pointers within 5 minutes after failover.
acceptance_criteria: Commit-fencing tokens are generated and validated; promotion rejected without a valid token
Forensic bundle schema v1 documented and output produced for every failover event
Bundles are signed and their checksums are stored in evidence-exporter; retrieval end-to-end verified in staging
Console shows geo-affinity gates and logs every override with operator identity
Automated tests cover token expiration, replay protection, and bundle signature verification
